questions.question: In March 2025, how many Light Combat Helicopters, Prachand, were ordered by the Ministry of Defence ?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**156**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ministry of Defence in March **2025** approved the procurement of **156 Light Combat Helicopters (LCH), Prachand**, under its modernization and indigenization efforts.
 
• The LCH, named **Prachand**, is an advanced indigenous helicopter designed and developed by **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**.
 
• This rotary-wing platform is specifically designed for **high-altitude operations** and supports roles such as **anti-tank warfare, combat search and rescue, and counter-insurgency operations**.
 
• The LCH is equipped with advanced features like **stealth, night attack capability, and armor protection**, making it suitable for modern warfare.
 
• It can operate in **extreme weather conditions** and is capable of engaging in combat even at altitudes of **15,000 feet**, making it ideal for operations in the **Ladakh region or similar high-altitude terrains**.
 
• This procurement aligns with the **'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (Self-Reliant India)** initiative, emphasizing indigenous defense production.
 
• The order reinforces the Indian Armed Forces' capability to handle **modern combat situations** effectively, particularly in challenging terrains like the Himalayas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand:**

 
 
• Designed and manufactured by **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**.
 
• It is the **world's lightest attack helicopter** in its category.
 
• Features include **stealth technology, a narrow fuselage, and crash-worthy landing gear.**
 
• Equipped with **advanced weapon systems** such as **air-to-air missiles, anti-tank guided missiles, 20mm turret guns, and rocket pods**.
 
• It is capable of **neutralizing enemy radar and surveillance systems**.
 
 
 
• This procurement further demonstrates India's growing focus on **indigenization and modernization** of its defense forces.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the 2024 Jharkhand Assembly elections is/are INCORRECT?

1. The Indian National Congress won more than 15 seats.

2. The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha won the highest vote share.

3. Rashtriya Janata Dal won 4 seats in the Assembly.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question pertains to the **2024 Jharkhand Assembly elections**, which are crucial for understanding the political landscape of Jharkhand.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because the claim that the **Indian National Congress won more than 15 seats** is factually inaccurate based on the results of the 2024 Jharkhand Assembly elections.
 
• Option 2 is incorrect as it asserts that the **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) won the highest vote share**, which is not the case. Another party might have held the highest vote share during these elections.
 
• Option 3 is correct as the **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)** winning 4 seats aligns with the results of the 2024 elections.
 
• The correct answer highlights that only the claims in Option 1 and Option 2 are incorrect, while Option 3 holds true.
 
• Understanding the dynamics of the 2024 Jharkhand Assembly elections is essential for evaluating the role of different parties such as the **Indian National Congress, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, and Rashtriya Janata Dal** in shaping the state’s governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• The **Indian National Congress**, founded in **1885**, is one of the oldest political parties in India.
 
• It played a significant role in the **Indian Independence Movement** and has been a major political force post-independence.
 
• The party advocates for **secularism, democracy, and socialism**.
 
• In recent elections, its performance has varied across states, reflecting changing political dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)**__
 __
 
• The **JMM** was established in **1972** by **Shibu Soren** to represent the interests of tribal communities in Jharkhand.
 
• The party has been a key player in Jharkhand politics and has led the government in the state multiple times.
 
• It advocates for **tribal rights, land reforms, and sustainable development**.
 
• JMM's political strength is concentrated in tribal-dominated regions of Jharkhand.
 
 
 
• **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)**__
 
 
• The **RJD** was founded in **1997** by **Lalu Prasad Yadav** and primarily operates in Bihar and Jharkhand.
 
• It is known for its focus on **social justice, caste-based politics, and empowering marginalized communities**.
 
• The party has historically been strong among **Yadavs and Muslims** in the region.
 
• While the RJD primarily focuses on Bihar, it also contests elections in Jharkhand, where it has a smaller but notable presence.

questions.question: In February 2025, which bank of India has announced $10 billion three-year dollar/rupee swap auction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, as the central bank of India, regularly conducts dollar-rupee swap auctions to manage liquidity and stabilize currency fluctuations.
 
• In February 2025, RBI announced a **$10 billion three-year dollar-rupee swap auction** aimed at enhancing liquidity management and providing stability to the foreign exchange market.
 
• Dollar-rupee swap auctions are a tool used by RBI to infuse liquidity in the Indian banking system by exchanging US dollars for Indian rupees with a promise to reverse the transaction in the future.
 
• Such auctions are critical for addressing short-term liquidity mismatches while ensuring the smooth functioning of financial markets.
 
• The move aligns with RBI's proactive measures to manage external risks and stabilize the value of the Indian rupee amidst global economic uncertainties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dollar-Rupee Swap Explained:**

 
 
• A dollar-rupee swap is a financial transaction where RBI buys US dollars from banks in exchange for rupees with an agreement to reverse the transaction at a future date.
 
• This mechanism helps in managing both liquidity and foreign exchange reserves efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Forex Swap Auctions:**
 
 
• Forex swaps ensure adequate liquidity in the banking system and reduce volatility in currency markets.
 
• They play a crucial role in balancing the demand and supply of foreign currency in the domestic market.
 
 
 
• **RBI's Role in Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• RBI uses various monetary tools such as repo rate, reverse repo rate, and forex swaps to regulate liquidity and inflation.
 
• Forex swaps complement these tools by addressing external sector risks and stabilizing exchange rates.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Financial Markets:**
 
 
• Such auctions are closely monitored by investors and banks as they impact liquidity, interest rates, and currency exchange rates.
 
• The announcement of a $10 billion swap auction reflects RBI's commitment to maintaining financial stability amidst global economic challenges.

questions.question: what was the size of the special economic and comprehensive package launched by the central government to fight COVID-19 pandemic in India
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹20 lakh crore**__.

 
• The central government of India announced a **₹20 lakh crore economic package** to combat the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• This package was part of the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (Self-Reliant India Campaign)**, announced by PM Narendra Modi in May 2020.
 
• The package aimed to provide relief to various sectors, including agriculture, small businesses, and migrant laborers, while boosting the economy.
 
• The initiative combined fiscal measures, monetary policy reforms, and liquidity support to address the short-term and long-term challenges posed by the pandemic.
 
• It accounted for approximately **10% of India's GDP** at the time, marking one of the largest stimulus packages announced globally.

 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan:**

 
 
• It is a campaign aimed at making India self-reliant by promoting local manufacturing, reducing import dependence, and boosting exports.
 
• The campaign focuses on five key pillars: economy, infrastructure, technology-driven systems, demography, and demand.
 
• It emphasized the "Vocal for Local" initiative to support domestic industries.
 
 
 
• **Breakdown of the ₹20 lakh crore package:**
 
 
• A large part of the package consisted of liquidity measures introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• Direct fiscal support from the government included cash transfers, free food grains distribution, and tax relief measures.
 
• Special provisions were made for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), agriculture, and healthcare infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 and Economic Challenges:**
 
 
• The pandemic disrupted supply chains, reduced consumer demand, and led to massive job losses, especially in the informal sector.
 
• The lockdown measures imposed to contain the virus significantly impacted industries such as hospitality, tourism, and retail.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison:**
 
 
• The ₹20 lakh crore package was among the largest globally in terms of GDP proportion, alongside stimulus measures by countries like the US and Japan.
 
• While India's package focused on long-term structural reforms, other nations prioritized direct fiscal transfers and immediate financial support.

questions.question: Which of the following was the theme of National Science Day 2025, celebrated on the 28th of February?

options.text: Fostering Scientific Excellence through Youth-Driven Research and Innovation in India
Empowering Indian Youth for Global Leadership in Science and Innovation for India's Bright Future
Advancing Scientific Vision through Innovation and Collaborative Growth in Bharat
Building a Developed Nation through Scientific Thinking and Modern Technology

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Empowering Indian Youth for Global Leadership in Science and Innovation for India's Bright Future**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The theme for National Science Day 2025 is **"Empowering Indian Youth for Global Leadership in Science and Innovation for India's Bright Future."**
 
• The focus of this theme is to **highlight the role of young minds in driving scientific research, innovation, and global leadership** in the field of science and technology.
 
• National Science Day is celebrated on **28th February every year** to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C.V. Raman in 1928.
 
• This theme aligns with the Indian government's vision of **promoting scientific excellence and innovation as key drivers of economic growth and national development.**
 
• Various activities such as seminars, exhibitions, and science fairs are conducted across schools, colleges, and research institutions to **raise awareness about the importance of science in daily life.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raman Effect:**

 
 
• Discovered by Indian physicist Sir C.V. Raman on February 28, 1928.
 
• It explains the scattering of light when it passes through a transparent medium, resulting in a change in its wavelength.
 
• This discovery earned C.V. Raman the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.**
 
 
 
• **Purpose of National Science Day:**
 
 
• To spread awareness about the importance of science in improving the quality of life.
 
• Encourages young minds to pursue careers in science and research.
 
 
 
• **Science and Youth Empowerment:**
 
 
• Youth-driven research and innovation play a crucial role in addressing global challenges such as climate change, health crises, and technological advancements.
 
• India’s National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 emphasizes **STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics)** education to foster innovation.
 
 
 
• **India's Global Leadership in Science:**
 
 
• India has emerged as a global leader in space exploration, biotechnology, and IT-driven innovations.
 
• Initiatives like **Startup India** and **Make in India** encourage scientific entrepreneurship among youth.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Theatre Level Operational Readiness Exercise (TROPEX-25) are correct?

1. TROPEX-25 is an annual exercise involving multiple Indian forces.

2. The exercise is being conducted in the Indian Ocean Region over a duration of three months.

3. The exercise includes participation from the Indian Army, Indian Air Force, and Indian Coast Guard.

4. The exercise focuses solely on cyber and electronic warfare operations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **TROPEX-23** is an annual exercise conducted by the Indian Navy to test its operational readiness across multiple domains.
 
• The exercise is conducted in the **Indian Ocean Region** over a duration of three months.
 
• TROPEX includes participation from the **Indian Army, Indian Air Force, and Indian Coast Guard**, showcasing integrated force capabilities.
 
• The exercise aims to evaluate operational strategies, enhance interoperability, and test readiness in conventional and non-conventional domains.
 
• The focus is on joint operations rather than solely cyber and electronic warfare, making it a comprehensive military drill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**

 
 
• The IOR is strategically significant due to its vast maritime trade routes and geopolitical importance.
 
• India conducts frequent naval exercises in the region to ensure maritime security and freedom of navigation.
 
 
 
• **Interoperability**
 
 
• Interoperability refers to the ability of different military forces to work together seamlessly.
 
• TROPEX emphasizes joint operations between the Navy, Army, Air Force, and Coast Guard.
 
 
 
• **Cyber Warfare**
 
 
• Cyber warfare involves the use of cyber attacks to disrupt, damage, or destroy adversary systems.
 
• While TROPEX includes cyber and electronic warfare elements, its scope is broader and includes conventional operations.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Military Strategy**
 
 
• TROPEX is a platform to test India's integrated military strategies and preparedness.
 
• Such exercises focus on enhancing force projection and defending national interests in maritime regions.

questions.question: As per the NITI Aayog Report titled 'FAST TRACKING FREIGHT IN INDIA' of 2021, what was the share of road transport in the freight traffic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.71**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the NITI Aayog report titled **'FAST TRACKING FREIGHT IN INDIA' (2021)**, the road transport sector accounted for **71% of the freight traffic in India**.
 
• This dominance of road transport is attributed to its flexibility, last-mile connectivity, and the rapid growth of e-commerce and logistics sectors.
 
• The share of railways in freight transport was significantly lower, emphasizing the need for a modal shift to reduce logistics costs and environmental impact.
 
• The report highlights the need for **improving multi-modal logistics** and enhancing the efficiency of rail, waterways, and air transport systems.
 
• With freight transport demand expected to grow rapidly, **road transport's share must be complemented by increased investment in sustainable alternatives**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freight Transport in India:**

 
 
• India's freight transport is dominated by roadways, followed by railways, inland waterways, and air transport.
 
• Freight traffic demand is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.9% between 2020 and 2050, as per NITI Aayog estimates.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Road Freight Transport:**
 
 
• High logistics costs: India's logistics costs are 13-14% of GDP, higher than developed countries' average of 8-10%.
 
• Environmental concerns: Road transport contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.
 
• Infrastructure bottlenecks: Lack of proper road infrastructure and congestion affect transport efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Proposed Solutions:**
 
 
• Shifting freight to rail and waterways to reduce costs and environmental impact.
 
• Development of multi-modal logistics parks to enhance connectivity and reduce transit times.
 
• Use of technology for efficient freight tracking and reduced delays.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Bharatmala Pariyojana aims to improve road infrastructure and connectivity across the country.
 
• The Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) project aims to enhance the efficiency and capacity of rail freight transport.
 
• Promotion of electric and alternative fuel vehicles to reduce the carbon footprint of road transport.

questions.question: What is the estimated monthly per capita household consumption expenditure in rural India, as reported by Household Consumption Expenditure Survey: 2023-24?

The correct answer is __**₹4,122**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The estimated monthly per capita household consumption expenditure in rural India is **₹4,122**, as per the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey: 2023-24.
 
• This survey is conducted periodically by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• It measures consumption expenditure patterns to assess the **standard of living** and economic well-being of households.
 
• The data serves as a basis for calculating important economic indicators, including the **Poverty Line** and Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• Rural consumption expenditure reflects household spending on essentials like food, housing, clothing, healthcare, education, and other goods and services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES)**

 
 
• It is a nationwide survey conducted every five years to collect data on household expenditure.
 
• The survey provides insights into the consumption habits of households across **rural and urban areas**.
 
• Key parameters include food items, non-food items, durable goods, and services.
 
• HCES data is used to estimate poverty levels, inequality, and **budgetary policies**.
 
 
 
• **Per Capita Household Expenditure**
 
 
• This metric is derived by dividing the total household expenditure by the number of members in the household.
 
• It is an important indicator of the **standard of living** and purchasing power of individuals.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Rural and Urban Consumption**
 
 
• Rural consumption is typically focused on necessities like food and basic services.
 
• Urban households spend more on discretionary items such as entertainment, electronics, and luxury goods.
 
 
 
• **Use of HCES Data**
 
 
• Data is used to design and evaluate government welfare programs like the **Public Distribution System (PDS)**.
 
• It helps in identifying **vulnerable groups** and framing poverty alleviation policies.
 
• It is crucial for economic planning and measuring inequality through indicators like the Gini coefficient.

questions.question: What was the name of India's humanitarian mission to provide assistance to Myanmar after the earthquake in March 2025?

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was India's humanitarian mission initiated to provide emergency relief to Myanmar following a devastating earthquake in March 2025.
 
• The operation aimed to deliver medical aid, food supplies, and search-and-rescue teams to affected regions of Myanmar.
 
• The mission was coordinated by the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** of India in collaboration with Myanmar's government.
 
• Specialized teams, including the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**, were deployed to assist in rescue operations and provide immediate relief.
 
• The operation highlighted India's commitment to regional humanitarian assistance and disaster response under its "Neighborhood First" policy.

• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**

 
 
• NDRF is a specialized force under the Ministry of Home Affairs in India, tasked with handling natural and human-made disasters.
 
• The force is equipped with advanced equipment and trained personnel for disaster management and rescue operations.
 
• NDRF played a pivotal role during Operation Brahma in Myanmar by conducting rescue missions and delivering relief materials.
 
 
 
• **Neighborhood First Policy**
 
 
• India's foreign policy emphasizes strengthening relations with neighboring countries through cooperation and mutual assistance.
 
• Under this policy, India provides humanitarian aid and disaster relief to neighboring nations during crises.
 
• Operation Brahma was a prime example of India's commitment to this policy.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake Disaster Management**
 
 
• Earthquakes are natural disasters requiring immediate response to minimize casualties and damage.
 
• Disaster management includes rescue operations, medical support, and rehabilitation for affected populations.
 
• India's NDMA and NDRF regularly train for earthquake-related disaster response, ensuring readiness for missions like Operation Brahma.
 
 
 
• **Humanitarian Assistance Operations**
 
 
• Humanitarian missions involve providing aid to countries facing natural or man-made disasters.
 
• Such operations often include delivering food, water, medicine, and shelter to affected populations.
 
• India has conducted several humanitarian assistance missions, including Operation Brahma, showcasing its leadership in regional disaster response.

questions.question: What was the main change introduced by the 2015 Amendment to the Citizenship Act?

options.text: Merged PIO and OCI card schemes
Created a new visa category for tourists

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,The 2015 Amendment to the Citizenship Act brought significant changes to simplify and consolidate the provisions related to Indian citizenship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2015 Amendment merged the **Person of Indian Origin (PIO)** and **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)** card schemes into a single category called OCI.
 
• This was introduced to eliminate confusion between the two schemes and simplify the application process for foreign nationals of Indian origin.
 
• OCI cardholders were granted several benefits, including **visa-free travel to India, exemption from registration with authorities, and access to certain economic and educational privileges.**
 
• The merger was intended to strengthen ties with the Indian diaspora by providing a streamlined and unified framework.
 
• The amendment also clarified eligibility criteria and procedures for obtaining OCI cards, making it more accessible for qualifying individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Person of Indian Origin (PIO) Card:**

 
 
• Introduced in 1999, the PIO card was issued to foreign nationals of Indian origin for facilitating long-term visa-free travel and residency in India.
 
• PIO cardholders had limited benefits compared to OCI cardholders, such as restrictions on employment and property acquisition.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Card:**
 
 
• OCI was introduced in 2005 as part of efforts to strengthen ties with the Indian diaspora.
 
• OCI cardholders enjoy more benefits than PIO cardholders, including lifelong visa-free travel and access to certain economic and educational opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Citizenship Act of 1955:**
 
 
• The Citizenship Act governs the acquisition, termination, and supplemental provisions of Indian citizenship.
 
• It has been amended several times to accommodate changing socio-political and global scenarios.
 
 
 
• **Indian Diaspora:**
 
 
• The Indian diaspora refers to people of Indian origin living outside India, estimated to be over 30 million globally.
 
• Government initiatives like OCI aim to foster connections and tap into the potential of this community.

questions.question: According to the Reserve Bank of India, as of October 2024, India became the fourth country whose foreign exchange (forex) reserves swelled to $_______ billion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**701**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of October 2024, India became the fourth country in the world to have foreign exchange (forex) reserves exceeding **$701 billion**.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is responsible for managing the country’s forex reserves, which include foreign currency assets, gold reserves, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and the reserve position in the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
 
• India’s forex reserves crossed the $700 billion mark, highlighting its strong economic fundamentals and resilience in the global financial landscape.
 
• Other countries with similar high forex reserves include China, Japan, and Switzerland.
 
• Maintaining high forex reserves is essential for stabilizing the Indian rupee and supporting India’s imports, external debt, and economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves**

 
 
• Forex reserves consist of foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs (Special Drawing Rights), and the reserve position in the IMF.
 
• These reserves act as a buffer against external economic shocks and ensure financial stability.
 
• They are critical for maintaining investor confidence and supporting the balance of payments.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**
 
 
• The RBI is India’s central bank, tasked with managing monetary policy, regulating banks, and overseeing the country’s forex reserves.
 
• It actively intervenes in the forex market to stabilize the Indian rupee against global currencies.
 
 
 
• **Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)**
 
 
• SDRs are supplementary foreign exchange reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
 
• They are based on a basket of major international currencies, including the US dollar, euro, yuan, yen, and pound sterling.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Forex Reserves**
 
 
• They enable a country to meet its external obligations, including import payments and debt repayments.
 
• High reserves help mitigate currency volatility and ensure economic stability during global financial crises.
 
 
 
• **India’s Forex History**
 
 
• India’s forex reserves have grown significantly since the economic liberalization of 1991, when they were critically low.
 
• In 2021, India’s forex reserves exceeded $600 billion for the first time, showcasing its economic progress.

questions.question:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with the beneficiaries of the 'Lakhpati Didi' scheme in Gujarat in March 2025. In this context, which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. The scheme aims to empower women by enabling SHG members to earn an annual household income of at least ₹1 lakh, sustained over agricultural seasons or business cycles.

2. It offers direct annual cash transfers of ₹1 lakh to selected SHG members to support their livelihoods.

3. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development under DAY-NRLM.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Lakhpati Didi' scheme aims to **empower women by enabling members of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to achieve an annual household income of at least ₹1 lakh**, sustained through agricultural seasons or business cycles.
 
• The scheme is implemented under the **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**, which is spearheaded by the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• It focuses on enhancing the livelihoods of rural women through entrepreneurial activities, capacity building, and access to financial resources.
 
• The scheme does not include direct annual cash transfers of ₹1 lakh to beneficiaries, but instead supports income generation via skill development and enterprise promotion.
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with the beneficiaries of the scheme in Gujarat in March 2025 to assess its impact on women empowerment and rural development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM):**

 
 
• Launched in 2011, DAY-NRLM aims to reduce poverty by enhancing sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural poor households.
 
• It focuses on creating efficient and effective institutional platforms for the rural poor, especially women, to enable them to increase household income through self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities.
 
• The mission promotes financial inclusion by linking SHGs to banks for credit support.
 
 
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):**
 
 
• SHGs are small, voluntary associations of people, typically women, who come together to save and collectively manage resources for income-generating activities.
 
• They play a significant role in empowering women and improving rural livelihoods.
 
 
 
• **Empowerment of Women through SHGs:**
 
 
• SHGs facilitate access to credit, skills training, and market linkages, enabling women to start and sustain micro-enterprises.
 
• The 'Lakhpati Didi' scheme is a prime example of leveraging SHGs for women’s economic empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of DAY-NRLM:**
 
 
• Universal social mobilization by bringing at least one woman from each identified rural poor household into SHG networks.
 
• Skill development and entrepreneurship promotion to enhance employability and income generation.

questions.question: According to the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2024, what is the projected global temperature rise by the end of the century if current policies continue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2024, current global policies are projected to result in a temperature rise of **3.1% by the end of the century**.
 
• This projection is based on the assumption that there will be no significant strengthening of climate mitigation policies globally.
 
• Limiting global warming to **below 2°C or ideally 1.5°C** as per the Paris Agreement requires enhanced efforts to close the emissions gap.
 
• The **emissions gap** refers to the difference between the global emissions required to meet climate targets and the emissions expected under current policies.
 
• UNEP reports highlight the urgent need for countries to implement stronger climate action to avoid catastrophic impacts on ecosystems and human societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paris Agreement:**

 
 
• The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, is an international treaty on climate change aimed at limiting global warming to well below 2°C and pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.
 
• It emphasizes nationally determined contributions (NDCs), where each country sets its climate goals.
 
 
 
• **Emissions Gap:**
 
 
• The emissions gap represents the shortfall between the greenhouse gas emissions reductions pledged by nations and the reductions needed to meet global climate targets.
 
• Closing the gap requires stronger national commitments, rapid decarbonization, and global cooperation.
 
 
 
• **UNEP:**
 
 
• The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is responsible for assessing global environmental challenges, including climate change.
 
• Its annual Emissions Gap Report evaluates the effectiveness of climate policies and highlights areas needing urgent action.
 
 
 
• **Global Impacts of Warming:**
 
 
• A temperature rise of 3.1% could lead to severe disruptions, including intensified heatwaves, flooding, droughts, and loss of biodiversity.
 
• Such warming would disproportionately affect vulnerable communities and exacerbate social inequalities.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the recent Supreme Court developments on bail under the PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002) in 2024-25?

1. The Supreme Court has clarified that prolonged incarceration without trial can be a valid ground for granting bail under PMLA-2002, despite the twin conditions under Section 45.

2. In Arvind Kejriwal’s case, the Court ruled that the legality of arrest must also consider the “need and necessity” of arrest, in addition to the standard “reasons to believe” clause.

3. The Court has held that “bail is the exception, jail the rule”, which remains applicable in money laundering cases.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Statements 1 and 2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The Supreme Court has clarified that prolonged incarceration without trial can be a valid ground for granting bail under PMLA-2002, despite the twin conditions under Section 45.
 
• **Statement 2:** In a recent judgment related to Arvind Kejriwal’s case, the Court emphasized that the legality of arrest must consider both the "need and necessity" of the arrest and the "reasons to believe" clause.
 
• **Statement 3:** Not correct. The Court did not declare "bail is the exception, jail the rule" as applicable to money laundering cases under PMLA.
 
• The correct interpretation of the Supreme Court’s developments on PMLA bail focuses on ensuring fair trial rights while balancing the stringent provisions of Section 45.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PMLA, 2002:** The Prevention of Money Laundering Act was enacted to prevent money laundering and confiscate property derived from such activities.
 
• **Section 45:** It imposes twin conditions for granting bail, requiring the court to be satisfied that (1) the accused is not guilty and (2) they are unlikely to commit any offense while on bail.
 
• **Prolonged Incarceration:** The Supreme Court has increasingly recognized that prolonged pre-trial detention violates the right to a fair and speedy trial under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Need and Necessity Test:** Introduced by the Supreme Court, this test evaluates whether an arrest is essential and proportionate, rather than routine, particularly in economic offenses.
 
• **Stringent Bail Laws:** The PMLA’s stringent provisions reflect the seriousness of money laundering offenses, which have cross-border implications and impact national security.
